route: Written approval of the Immigration Board

permit.applies: the sponsor, who by the Board's policy is the employer, resident in American Samoa
permit.first: a resident sponsor (an American Samoan or US national, or a firm authorised to do business there) and the Board's being satisfied of the need and of the lack of permanent residents for the work, within the numerical limitations

fees.what: application fee, temporary or seasonal workers (A.S.A.C. 41.0319(b)(4))

permit.eligibility: Persons may be sponsored for purposes of other employment provided the Board is satisfied of the need and of the lack of permanent residents for such employment, and the person is within the numerical limitations established in chapter 03.

sources.title: American Samoa Bar Association, A.S.A.C. 41.1005 Employment of aliens
sources.said: (a) No person may knowingly employ any alien without written approval before the person commences work. (b) No alien may seek employment or become employed without prior written approval of the office or the board. … (d) It is the policy of the immigration board that the employer shall be the sponsor of all alien employees unless a sufficient reason should appear to the board for allowing another person to sponsor the alien.

sources.title: American Samoa Bar Association, A.S.C.A. 41.0408 Sponsors
sources.said: (a) Every person who applies for permission from the Board to remain in American Samoa is required to have a sponsor. (b) The following persons are eligible to act as sponsor: (1) all American Samoans, and nationals of the United States; (2) any partnership or corporation authorized to do business in American Samoa. … (d) Persons may be sponsored for purposes of other employment provided the Board is satisfied of the need and of the lack of permanent residents for such employment, and the person is within the numerical limitations established in chapter 03.

sources.title: American Samoa Bar Association, A.S.A.C. 41.0319 Fees
sources.said: (b) Amounts of fees. The following fees and charges are prescribed: … (4) a fee of $15 shall be charged for the following application: temporary or seasonal workers; … History: Rule 3-86. eff 7 Dec 86.

sources.title: American Samoa Bar Association, A.S.A.C. 41.0409 Bonds
sources.said: (a) The Attorney General or chief immigration officer may in his/her discretion, require any alien who is either visiting or residing in American Samoa to post a cash bond, to ensure that she/he will not become a financial burden to the American Samoa Government, not to exceed an amount sufficient to pay transportation costs to his/her home country plus not more than $500.

note: American Samoa's own code and rules (A.S.C.A. Title 41, A.S.A.C. Title 41, read in the American Samoa Bar Association's copies). The fee is the temporary or seasonal worker's application fee of Rule 3-86 (1986), the latest the Bar's copy holds; a cash bond of up to the fare home plus $500 may be required at the Attorney General's discretion and is a deposit, not a fee. No union step, minimum pay or exempt days are named in the chapters read. The chapter 09 guest worker permit (cannery and call-centre workers) isn't a performer's route.
